relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.evidence: Use the `channel()` function to route the document to the named channel(s).

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.evidence: A channel implicitly comes into existence when a document is routed to it.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.evidence: Couchbase Sync Gateway defines a Sync Function at the `collection` level. Defining at this level helps simplify data management and improve data reliability. Each collection in the system allows for only one Sync Function, which enables the specification of Access Control rules.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.evidence: By default, every document in the collection is automatically assigned to a channel with the same name as the collection. This system automatically creates a channel with the collection's name.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no promoted predicate captures 'a side effect is provisional until the write actually commits'; distinct from doesNotSatisfy/doesNotSupport (both about grants, not about commit-timing) and from hasExecutionConstraint (deliberately scoped to topology/placement only, per that relation's own promotion note)
relations.evidence: Routing changes have no effect until the document is actually saved in the database, so if the sync function first calls `channel()` or `access()`, but then rejects the update, the channel and access changes will not occur.

cross_component_finding: This is the fullest first-hand statement in the batch of a rejection-semantics rule shared by channel() and access(): routing/grant side effects are provisional and are discarded together if the sync function goes on to reject the update (via throw() or any require*() check throwing). This directly connects the two 'mutate the access graph' helpers (channel(), access()) to the 'gate the write' helpers (throw(), requireRole(), requireUser(), requireAccess(), requireAdmin()) documented elsewhere in this same batch: all of them execute within one all-or-nothing sync-function invocation per document revision, and only a fully-accepted revision's channel()/access() calls actually take effect.
